title: Gangnam Dream
description:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.

Five years ago, there were nights in a goshiwon room, buried under a blanket, staring at a phone screen at dawn.
Gangnam — three billion. A number so big it was almost funny.

Now {name} stands in that living room, the city laid out below the big window.

The doorbell rings. It's his father.
He opens the door. Hands worn from a lifetime in a factory, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and stared out the window for a long while.
He didn't say a word. Just looked.

Then, quietly, he said.
"...It's good, son."

{name} couldn't say anything.
Six years of debt and five years of struggle were all packed into those few words.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at Gangnam at night.

It wasn't winning.
He just — hadn't lost.

description_if_known.sangchul_truth_buried:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.

Now {name} stands in that living room, the city laid out below the big window.

The doorbell rings. It's his father.
He opens the door. Hands worn from a lifetime in a factory, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and stared out the window for a long while.
Then, quietly, he said.
"...It's good, son."

{name} couldn't say anything.

His father doesn't know.
That half of the view out this window passed through the hands of the man who ruined him.
That day at the cafe, {name} had said, "Forget it. Let it go."
With those few words he buried his father's debt, and himself, together.

Now the thing he'd buried — seemed to be watching the night view from somewhere in this living room too.

"It is good, Dad."
{name} said only that.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at Gangnam at night.
His father was smiling, to the very end.
description_if_known.sangchul_forgiven:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.

Now {name} stands in that living room, the city laid out below the big window.

The doorbell rings. It's his father.
He opens the door. Hands worn from a lifetime in a factory, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and stared out the window for a long while.
Then, quietly, he said.
"...It's good, son."

{name} thought of Lim Sang-chul.
The day he knew the truth and, instead of reporting him, said "Those few words were enough."
Maybe it wasn't forgiveness — maybe he just had no strength left to spend on hating.

Still, because of that choice, he could call his father here today.
In the hand that set down its resentment — there was a deed.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at Gangnam at night.

It wasn't winning.
He'd just — stopped hating anyone anymore.
description_if_known.sangchul_quietly_distanced:
Three billion won.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.

Now {name} stands in that living room, the city laid out below the big window.

The doorbell rings. It's his father.
He opens the door. Hands worn from a lifetime in a factory, shoulders bent.

His father came into the living room and stared out the window for a long while.
Then, quietly, he said.
"...It's good, son."

{name} thought of Lim Sang-chul.
After walking out of that cafe without a word, he never reached out again.
The information Sang-chul fed him, the network, the seats — he left all of it behind.

He knows that made the road to Gangnam many times longer.
But {name} knows that nowhere in this view out the window did that man's hand reach.

This was wholly {name}'s own.

The two of them stood side by side, looking at Gangnam at night.

It wasn't winning.
But at least — he hadn't borrowed it.

title: Empty House
description:
A Gangnam apartment.
{name}'s name is printed on the deed.

He reached the goal.

But there's no one to show it to.

Last winter, his father slipped away quietly while hospitalized.
That call where he'd said 'I'll definitely come down next month' — was the last.

A wide living room. A big window. A night view with no one in it.
{name} sat on the sofa and stared at that window for a long time.

He'd wanted to show his father.
That had been the real reason from the very start.

Where that reason used to be — there's a three-billion-won house.

title: With Dae-eun
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

But he has Dae-eun.

A rented villa on the outskirts. The two of them barely getting by on what they earn.
On weekends they boil ramen, just like that first time they met at the convenience store.

Dae-eun picks up her chopsticks and asks.
"No regrets? About Gangnam."

{name} thought for a moment.
The overtime, the failed investments, the goshiwon fridge, all of it.

"I don't know. But right now — I'm not unhappy."

Dae-eun smiles.

Gangnam was the destination.
But maybe it was a destination he'd set when he didn't yet know what he really wanted.

The ramen was going cold. Neither of them ate. It was okay.

title: Jiyeon's Man
description:
He made it to Gangnam. With Han Jiyeon.

A good car, a good house, good people.
At her family's place, his father-in-law now calls {name} 'our son-in-law.'

One night, he stood alone in front of the bathroom mirror.

The man who rode a bicycle around the goshiwon five years ago.
The man who made a triangle kimbap his dinner.
Whether that man and {name} now are the same person — he doesn't know.

He lives in Gangnam.
But whether this is the Gangnam he wanted,
or whether he just moved into the Gangnam Jiyeon already lived in —

Jiyeon knocks on the bathroom door. "You up?"
"Yeah."

The door opens. She stands beside him. The two of them reflected in the mirror.

{name} smiled.
A happy smile, but one with something hollow in it.

title: Jaehyuk's Way
description:
He made it to Gangnam. Fast. Dirty.

He sold other people's information, exploited rivals' weaknesses,
broke promises more times than he could count.

The house he bought with that money.

He invited his father. His father was delighted.
"Wow, amazing. My son."

{name} couldn't smile at those words.

Because the faces he'd trampled on the way up
seemed to be standing right behind his father.

The people he'd hated so much.
And himself, now.

The living room of a Gangnam apartment. The city glittering outside the window.

{name} looked at that light for a while, then drew the curtains.

description_if_known.sangchul_used_fully:
He made it to Gangnam. Fast. Dirty.

Lim Sang-chul. The man who pushed his father into that debt.
Instead of cutting him off, {name} used his guilt as an asset.
He took the information, got introduced to the seats, was never refused.

The house he bought with that money.

He invited his father. His father was delighted.
"Wow, amazing. My son."

{name} couldn't smile at those words.
His father doesn't know whose hands this house passed through.

He remembered something Lim Sang-chul once said.
"You're like me."

Back then he'd wanted to deny it. Now — there was nothing to deny.
He started out hating him, and ended up exactly him.

The living room of a Gangnam apartment. The city glittering outside.
{name} looked at that light for a while, then drew the curtains.

title: The Late Call
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

The scenery streams past the KTX window. Bound for Changwon.
He'd struggled for five years, but Gangnam stayed out of reach in the end.

But with the phone in his hand, he calls his father.

"Dad, I'm coming down. Let's get a meal together."
The dial tone rang twice.

"...Sure. Dad'll buy you gukbap."

Raindrops gathered on the window.
{name} took out his earphones and pressed the phone closer to his ear.

He couldn't buy the Gangnam apartment.
Instead, he made this call he'd put off and put off for five years.

Maybe this was where he'd really wanted to go all along.

description_if_known.sangchul_used_fully:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

The scenery streams past the KTX window. Bound for Changwon.
He ran five years using Lim Sang-chul's guilt as a lever, and in the end Gangnam stayed out of reach.

He used him to the last. Took the information, got introduced to the seats.
And after all that — this is all there is.

With the phone in his hand, he calls his father.

"Dad, I'm coming down. Let's get a meal together."
The dial tone rang twice.

"...Sure. Dad'll buy you gukbap."

Listening to that voice, {name} thought.
That he'd used, with his own hands, the man who brought his father down —
he would never be able to say it through this call.

He sold everything there was to sell, and Gangnam never came.
What's left — a bowl of gukbap, and one thing he can never say.
description_if_known.sangchul_truth_known:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

The scenery streams past the KTX window. Bound for Changwon.
He'd struggled for five years, but Gangnam stayed out of reach in the end.

With the phone in his hand, he calls his father.

"Dad, I'm coming down. Let's get a meal together."
The dial tone rang twice.

"...Sure. Dad'll buy you gukbap."

{name} thought of Lim Sang-chul.
The man who pushed his father into that debt. {name} knows the truth.
His father doesn't.

He thought about telling him, hundreds of times.
But the voice on the other end right now — was just giddy that his son was coming down.

He didn't want to break that gladness.

He couldn't buy the Gangnam apartment.
Instead, so his father could stay at peace not knowing — {name} chose to carry that truth alone.

Maybe this was harder than Gangnam.

title: Stable Success
description:
One billion won.

The day that number first showed up in his account,
{name} did nothing.

He just closed the app and lay down to sleep.

Seoul glittered beyond the window.
Gangnam was somewhere in those lights. Out of reach.
And yet — he wasn't afraid.

Lease expirations, medical bills, payday texts.
Where all that weight used to be, a question settled in for the first time.

How should I live now.

He didn't reach three billion. He didn't achieve the Gangnam dream.
But waking up without fear —

maybe that was the real dream all along.

description_if_known.cut_sangchul_network:
The day one billion showed up in his account, {name} did nothing.
He just closed the app and lay down to sleep.

There were opportunities he'd passed on. Money that could have come faster. Deals he chose not to make.

The day he severed that connection came back to him. After that, things slowed.
For a long time it felt like a mistake.

But this one billion — it's money that never used anyone's guilt as leverage.
It came slowly. It's his money.

Seoul glittered beyond the window. He wasn't afraid.

title: Just a Person
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

A villa on the outskirts of Seoul. Rent 580,000 a month.
One room with one window, and beyond the window, the wall of the next building.

An ordinary job. An ordinary today.
Subway in the morning, subway in the evening, home to wash up and sleep.

Sometimes when Gangnam apartment prices come up on the news, he blanks out for a second.
'If I'd done things differently.' That thought comes too, sometimes.

But dinner tasted good tonight.
A cup ramen bought at the convenience store on the way home.
Rain falling outside, and it's his own room.

{name} went to search something on his phone, then just set it down.

In Seoul, there are far more people who didn't make it to Gangnam than people who did.
{name} is one of them.

Whether that's failure — he doesn't know.
What's certain is that tonight isn't cold.
There are nights when that's enough.

description_if_known.cut_sangchul_network:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

A villa on the outskirts of Seoul. Rent 580,000 a month.
One room, one window, and beyond it — the wall of the next building.

There was a door he could have walked through faster. He closed it.
Because he knew where that door came from.

Sometimes he wonders where he'd be now if he hadn't. Probably somewhere better.

But that thought doesn't stay long.
This room needs no explanation.

This room feeling a little less bitter — that's because of that choice.

title: Collapsed from Overwork
description:
His body stopped first.

It was on the goshiwon stairs. Coming down from the 3rd floor to the 1st,
he couldn't stay standing without gripping the railing.

There had been signs. Less sleep, skipped meals,
the room spinning every time he went to the bathroom.
Still he didn't stop. Seoul doesn't wait for people who rest.

An ER IV drip. Fluorescent lights on the ceiling.
Someone groaning in the next bed.

A nurse asked, checking the chart.
"Do you have a guardian's contact?"

{name} couldn't answer.
There were people he could call, but they were people he didn't want to call.
Father, mother, army buddies.
He didn't want to worry them. Because he hadn't achieved anything yet.

Gangnam was the goal.
While running, he lost the runner himself.

Staring at the hospital ceiling, he asked for the first time.

Am I, right now — happy.

No answer came.
Maybe he'd been the one not letting it come.

title: Mental Collapse
description:
The psychiatrist's office was quieter than he'd expected.

He'd held out three weeks before booking the appointment.
He hated going outside. He hated people.
At some point even getting up began to use all his energy.

The doctor asked. "What's the hardest thing for you these days?"

{name} thought for a moment.
He couldn't say 'I can't get to Gangnam.'
It didn't even seem like the real problem.

"I don't know. Everything just feels like too much."

He doesn't know when it started.
He wore out from comparing, collapsed from wearing out, didn't even notice he was collapsing.

He thought he had to act strong.
He thought weak people get pushed aside in Seoul.

That thought was wrong.

More precisely — even if it was right,
he couldn't survive five years that way.

Next time, the mind comes first. Before Gangnam.

title: Debt Abyss
description:
The day his debt passed 100 million, {name} decided to stop looking at the numbers.

At first it was a small minus.
He thought 'just for a moment.'
That became 20 million, 50 million, 100 million.

Leverage doubles your gains.
And it doubles your losses at the same ratio.
His head knew it. His hands didn't.

When the first collection call came, it was an unknown number, so he hung up.
The second, he answered then hung up.
The third, he just answered.

He sat in the goshiwon room punching at a calculator.
Principal 120 million. Monthly interest 950,000. Salary 2.2 million.

The numbers didn't add up.
He decided not to trace where it went wrong anymore.

He went out and bought a convenience store coffee.
500 won. That was exactly all that was in his wallet.

He started with 500,000.
He ended at minus 120 million.

Still, he starts again.
This time — beginning with not losing.

title: Crypto Ghost
description:
He could no longer put the phone down.

Watching crypto charts became the center of his life.
Cheering when it rose, crumbling when it fell.
At some point reality became the game, and the chart became reality.

He checked the screen even while eating.
He refreshed the order book even as he lay down to sleep.

The man who set out to buy a Gangnam apartment ended up spending his days with an exchange app in his hand.

The chart was right there. Life was somewhere else.

title: Startup Exit
description:
He signed the contract.

His hand still trembled a little.

The day he raised funding, the night a teammate ran off, the dawn he decided to pivot.
All of it got settled with this one signature.

The acquisition amount appeared as a number.

{name} went to the bathroom and washed his hands.
He stood in front of the mirror and did nothing for about ten seconds.

He came out.

As CEO, he sent a notice to the team.
"Thank you all for your hard work."

There wasn't just one way to buy a Gangnam apartment.
The world recognizing the value of what you built — that was a Gangnam dream too.

title: To Yeouido
description:
He was elected.

The man who set out to enter Gangnam entered Yeouido instead.
Starting from a goshiwon, through being an aide, all the way to the gold badge.

The day he first walked into the National Assembly member's office,
he could look down on the Gangnam apartment complexes through the window.

Five years ago he'd set out to live in that neighborhood.
Now he looks down on it.

His assets aren't three billion.
But that money isn't the only power in this city,
{name} proved in a different way.

The shape of a dream sometimes changes along the road.

title: The Lonely Rich
description:
One billion won showed up.

He sat alone in the living room and looked out the window.
Seoul at night was always beautiful.

He was hungry. He opened the delivery app, then closed it.
Eating alone felt like a hassle.

He opened his contacts.
He couldn't remember the last time he'd texted anyone 'Have you eaten?'

It wasn't that people left while he chased money.
More precisely, the moments he chose money over people had quietly piled up.

He opened the delivery app again.
Ordered a single portion.

A billion-won loneliness was — just loneliness.

title: Investment Master
description:
One day, he bought when others sold in fear.

He was right.

The next time too.
And the next.

At first he thought it was luck.
When it kept repeating, a pattern began to show.

The market moves on people's emotions.
It gets cheap when people are afraid, expensive when they're greedy.
{name} walked the opposite direction in that current.

Five hundred million.

This money wasn't born.
The practice of admitting when he was wrong,
the practice of not crumbling when he lost,
those hours piled up into it.

He gained something worth more than money.
An eye that reads the market.
No one can take this away.

title: Legend of Seoul
description:
He doesn't know when it started.

One day he went to an industry event, and a stranger knew his name first.
"You're {name}, aren't you?"

{name} paused for a moment.

Trust breaks if you rush it.
He kept promises, did what he said, admitted when he didn't know.
That was all.

But it added up.

Three hundred million. It wasn't Gangnam.
But in this city, {name}'s name came to mean the same thing as trust.

Seoul is, in the end, a city made of people.
{name} found a way to survive among those people for a long time.

title: Healthy Retirement
description:
Fifty-five. A morning jog.

His knees are still okay.
Running along the Han River, he stopped for a moment to look at the water.

He thought of the alley visible from a thirty-three-year-old's goshiwon window.
From that window he'd dreamed of Gangnam.

He didn't make it to Gangnam.

Instead, at fifty-five his knees are good, his blood pressure is normal, and he can run alone in the morning.
He didn't overdo it, he rested well, ate what he should and slept when he should.

The Han River was shining.

He learned early that running long requires a pace.
This is the result of that pace.

title: The Debt Spiral
description:
He sat in the goshiwon room punching at a calculator.

Principal 200 million. Monthly interest 1.4 million. Salary 2.5 million.

The numbers didn't add up. He borrowed more to pay, borrowed more to plug the gap.
Debt births interest, interest births debt.
The structure never added up from the start.

{name} set down the calculator.

He decided not to calculate anymore.
Where it went wrong — that no longer mattered.

He went out and bought a convenience store coffee.
500 won. That was exactly all that was in his wallet.

title: Pinnacle of the Orthodox
description:
He lived diligently.

While others struck it rich on crypto, he worked quietly.
He didn't refuse overtime, didn't skip company dinners, didn't talk back to his boss.

Two hundred million. It wasn't Gangnam.
But now he'd become someone others envied.

At a team dinner, a junior asked.
"How did you live so diligently, senior?"

{name} thought for a moment.

Whether he'd lived diligently.
Or — whether he'd been too afraid of other roads to leave this one.

"Just did." That's how he answered.

{name} himself still doesn't know the difference between the two.
Maybe that's the answer of this road.

title: Hollow Success
description:
At fifty-five he opened his bankbook.

The number was enough.

He stared out the window for a long while. He felt nothing.

He lived diligently. The way society wanted.
Didn't skip overtime, invested safely, didn't do anything that stood out.
Because that was right — no, more precisely, because people said it was right.

He never once asked what he himself wanted.

Is this success.
It's success, alright. Numbers don't lie.

But in this living room, who am I now.
That — there's no answer.

title: My Own Balance
description:
It was a road neither orthodox nor unorthodox.

He invested while working at a company,
did side gigs while investing,
refocused on the company when the side gigs went well.

Some people said you couldn't pin him down.

On one side, 'should have focused more,'
on the other, 'maybe spread too thin' — there were such moments.

But {name} was just — that was me.

He didn't make it to Gangnam.
Didn't succeed big, didn't fail big.

One evening, before the account balance,
he started thinking about whether today had been fun.

That was {name}'s way. He lived his own way, and survived.

description_if_known.cut_sangchul_network:
Balance meant — not just how much you bring in, but also what you choose not to bring in.

There was a connection he walked away from. A faster road, but he knew where it came from.

After that, things slowed. Still, he got here.

He didn't make it to Gangnam.
But none of this money has an origin he can't explain.

That was {name}'s balance.

title: The Outsider's Victory
description:
Five hundred million.

Down the road others laughed at.

While those who followed the orthodox path gained stability,
{name} was walking in a different direction.

The day he was nearly swept away by leverage.
The day a failed investment sent him back to the goshiwon.
Why he didn't change direction even then — honestly, he doesn't really know.

That road just didn't seem like his road.

Seoul is a city you have to fight to the end.
{name} survived that fight his own way.

Five years ago, a thirty-three-year-old staring at a bankbook in a goshiwon
wouldn't have believed this number if he'd seen it now.

He wouldn't have believed it. Which made it even better.

title: Early Retirement
description:
The alarm didn't go off.

He opened his eyes. It was morning.
Something felt off, so he checked his phone. No alarm.

Oh, right.

He retired before fifty.

He understood compounding early, put principle before greed,
and luck followed maybe twice.

The result was a 'morning without an alarm.'

He brewed coffee. Looked out the window.
Seoul was busy again today. People commuting, the subway, buses.

Five years ago he was out there.

Now he's here.

They say real life begins now.
{name} still doesn't know what that means.
He'll find out now. Without rushing.

title: The Age of the Creator
description:
The comment notifications wouldn't stop.

One million.
One million subscribers.

The day he uploaded his first video, it had 43 views.
That wasn't embarrassing. He just wanted to film.

That became 10,000, became 100,000, and now it's come this far.

A brand deal contract came in.
An amount more than a month's rent on a Gangnam apartment.

Signing it, {name} had a strange feeling.
Doing what he wanted to do, and the money followed.

He didn't know this kind of way existed five years ago.

There wasn't just one way to survive in Seoul.
{name} standing in front of the camera is the proof.

title: Myth
description:
Five hundred thousand won.
Three months.
Three billion.

It's a number that makes no sense. {name} himself knows it.

Whether it was at the racetrack or in front of a chart — only {name} knows what happened that day.
The odds that day, the bet that day. He could never do it again.

The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in his hand.
It came so fast that none of it feels real.

He still hasn't reconciled with his father.
He still hasn't met the people he was meant to meet.
A whole five years were still left.

And yet it's over. Because he reached the goal.

People will tell this story for years.
'A jobless guy living in a goshiwon got to Gangnam in three months.'
No one will believe it.

Seoul sometimes allows one impossible thing like this.
Who it'll be — no one knows.

— You found a path that was never designed.
This almost never happens.

title: In His Father's Name
description:
On the day he entered Gangnam, he called his father.
'Dad, that debt to the Lim guy — I paid it all off.'
A brief silence.
'...How?'
'From the man himself.'

His father was quiet for a long time, then wept.

Minjun looked out the window. It was Gangnam. The same sky as the day he first arrived.

title: Human Until Gangnam
description:
₩3 billion.
The deed to a Gangnam apartment, in hand.

In this city — no one was stepped on to get here.
This number once seemed impossible without exploitation.

It was, in fact, nearly impossible.
Slow. Many days felt like falling behind.
And yet — here.

Standing at the window. The Gangnam boulevard stretches below.
The same sky as the day {name} first arrived in this city, five years ago.

Back then, {name} was no one yet.
Now — {name} knows what was kept intact on the way here.

What that is worth, you only know by arriving.

title: To Gangnam, Together
description:
On the Gangnam apartment balcony, Dae-eun looked at the night view.
'It's really high up here.'
Minjun said, 'At first, getting here was the goal.'
Dae-eun turned around. 'And now?'

Minjun didn't answer. Instead he made another cup of coffee.

There are things that need no answer.

title: The Things He Kept
description:
On the day his father was discharged, Minjun went down to Changwon.

In the hospital parking lot, his father said.
'Don't you have to go back to Seoul?'
'I'll stay a while.'

Minjun carried his father's bags.
There was no Gangnam yet. There was something to do before that.

title: The End of the Circles
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

The bankbook fell far short of the goal.
The three billion he'd set five years ago remained, in the end, only a number.

But on {name}'s desk hangs a calendar.
A calendar full of circles.

Days spent without gambling. More than a hundred circles.

There was a time {name} hit rock bottom.
Blowing borrowed money, calculating the next hand at dawn.
There, he reached out a hand. Asking for help.

That was the best thing he did in these five years.

In terms of money it may be a lost game.
But not losing himself — that was something three billion couldn't buy.

{name} drew one more circle on the calendar today.
He'll draw one tomorrow too. That's enough.

title: The Ladder He Switched
description:
His business card changed three times.

Five years ago, he started at a convenience store night counter.
Next was an office job, then a bigger company, and now — a place you'd know by name.

Others said holding one position was a virtue.
{name} thought differently. Holding on and being trapped are different things.

The day he named a number first at the salary negotiation table,
the day he listened to the headhunter's call to the end instead of hanging up,
the day his hand didn't tremble as he handed in his resignation.

Those days piled up into his current title.

He couldn't buy a Gangnam apartment. Three billion was far off.
But {name} proved his worth to the market,
and that worth rose every year.

On the way home, he saw his reflection in the building lobby glass.
The suit didn't feel awkward.

He hadn't climbed a ladder.
He'd kept switching to a better one.

title: The Things He Endured
description:
The commuter bus. The dark city passing by the window.

He worked for five years.
He considered changing jobs, and actually moved, or tried to.
There were days he first spoke the word burnout out loud.
He moved toward something better, and there were days he moved out of exhaustion.

Thirty-eight. He has a job.
It's not three billion, and not even a hundred million.

Every time the bus passed a stop, he thought.
Is this failure.

For five years he never once gave up.
He didn't go bankrupt. He didn't collapse.
He didn't run away, and tried to find a better place.

Just because that doesn't all show up in his account balance now
— doesn't make it a lie.

The bus stopped at the last stop.
{name} rose from his seat and walked toward the door.

He goes to work tomorrow too.
Whether that's tragedy or relief — right now he isn't sure.

title: Reckoning
description:
He didn't make it to Gangnam.

Instead, he wrote a statement at the police station.
Park Sang-jin. Lim Sang-chul. The two names that brought down his father six years ago.

The hand writing the statement trembled.
Because he knew that the moment he wrote it, the last ladder to Gangnam would be pulled away.
Lim Sang-chul's network, the information he provided, those seats — all of it, over.

Still he didn't stop the pen.

He came home and called his father.
"Dad. About that debt. It's not your fault anymore. I looked into all of it."

The other end of the line was quiet for a long time.
And then his father, for the first time in his life, cried like a child.

There was no Gangnam apartment.
But that one phone call let him set down something heavier than six years of debt.

{name} opened the window.
Today, even the sky over Gangnam was just sky.

title: The Chronicler
description:
A story that began at thirty-three, in a goshiwon room.
He didn't reach Gangnam. Not three billion, not an apartment. At thirty-eight he still lived in a {housing}.

But one day, he began to write — everything that had happened.

Convenience store lunchboxes and 3 a.m., the first paycheck and the failed villa lease, a friend's wedding invitation and the New Year's rice cake soup eaten alone. The stock charts he pored over through sleepless nights, and the bathroom at the end of the goshiwon hall.

A memoir of a failed Gangnam dream.

First printing 50,000 copies. Number-one bestseller two weeks after release.
